item.title: Log Of Anomalous Items: Some edit suggestions
item.content:encoded:
Just going through this article again! I noticed a couple of grammatical mistakes, so I thought I'd suggest them here, along with some other changes. I'm suggesting them here because the article's locked, and I can't make them myself. I am by no means a professional, so I might not always be accurate.

+ Editing suggestions
- This is way longer than I thought it'd be

with David Byrne repeating the line and looking increasingly distraught as hands grip his head.

This line should probably say his hands grip his head, unless the author wanted to imply that there were several disembodied hands present.

Current Status: … Well, heh, looks like… w-was dad really like that? … I need to go lie down… *wimper*

"wimper" should be spelled Whimper.

A Carl Thompson Rainbow Bass. When any song of the band Primus is played, a voice is heard saying "Primus Sucks!"

There should probably be an "on it" after the played.

Item Description: A piece of paper. Descriptions of the item will transform the texts medium into paper.

"Texts" should be spelled with an apostrophe.

Individuals witnessing the resulting effect from this item will feel a strong urge to support the item, usually by compliments.

I feel like the additional "from this item" is unnecessary. The description feels clunkier with that in there. Also, just saying "support" is a little vague for foundation protocol. I think inserting something like "provide the object with emotional support" would make more sense.

that will play any song, with vocals in Kurt Donald Cobain's voice.

The comma there is unnecessary.

Despite the soft appearance,

The "the" should be an its.

will indicate that illegal contraband exist within its conpartments,

The "exist" should be plural.

As much as a small drag of a fingernail along the phone, top to bottom,

This sentence feels very clunky. Removing both commas and inserting "from" before "top to bottom" should help a little.

that show stylized logo of various GoI in

"logo" should be plural.

woman in the painting appear to staring at whoever is loo

Should be "appears" and "be staring"

A white glass plate seven inches in diameter where anything eaten from it is given a strong taste of salt, even if it did not contain any.

This doesn't read Foundation to me at all. I'd suggest rewording the description to something like this: "A white glass plate seven inches in diameter. Any food eaten off of it tastes strongly of salt, even if none was used in its cooking."

A .55 calibre bullet with the date of manufacture as 8/2/1898. The bullet was carbon dated back to 1898 being the only of it's kind created back then. The bullet can be fired an innumerous amount of times.

Same with this one. I'd try changing it to something like "A .55 calibre bullet. Carbon dating suggests it was manufactured in 1898. As no other ammunition manufactured back then matches this object's type, it is assumed to be one of a kind. The bullet can be fired an infinite amount of times without being spent."

That's all I could find for now! I'm fairly new, so if anything I suggested was unwarranted or incorrect, please let me know! Hope this helps.

item.title: SCP-3016:
item.content:encoded:
As many I liked the concept, but for me there are several things that in the end made it a downvote:

1- The wording problems CannedBread commented on are still all over the place and they're glaring. In a pseudo-scientific article this harms immersion and compound to other issues;

2- For me the containment breach is way over the top (pun intended). Not that I think people shouldn't like over the top breaches (I don't), but in this particular case I think it kinda sidetracks the narrative more than it should. You don't need Hell on Earth here, just a power shortage, and this can be achieved through fairly simpler events;

3- Likewise the triggering event could be made simpler, for similar reasons. All you need is a gas leak into the vacuum chamber (a vacuum chamber that didn't needed to be specially resistant by the way, so its integrity could be another source of embezzlement);

4- I feel that there could be a little more happening in the logs. It is one of the main points of the article and, although it conveys everything it needs to, as a narrative I felt it could be more. Not much, it isn't a question of making it unnecessarily big, just a few more details on the chamber?;

5- You don't need to ascribe to unnecessary harshness in Foundation treatment of other, I do not either, but this level of catastrophic embezzlement certainly would call for something other than wasting further more resources relocating this guy in the larger society (even if as a beggar). I do think highly educated and well trained D-Classes are on short supply.

TL;DR: You need to clean the text and focus your narrative. Do not waste time with big shenanigans that have no bearing with your story. And do not shy from being harsh on someone who caused actual damage.

Personally I would also put a limit on this thing (air resistance should put a practical limit despite continuous torque) and keep the floor a not-so-high temperature to give more space for the log. 200 C° is already quite inhabitable but still explorable.

item.title: Decisions We Make:
item.content:encoded: Very sweet, and I like that Sasha's relationship to her family has been developed a bit. For the record, I like that last name Merlo better than Grimmer, but something told me (to use an outdated and perhaps slightly insensitive saying) Sasha "wore the pants" in the relationship to the point that I was almost sure Gabe took her name. Tradition dies hard, I guess, heheh. It's just funny. I didn't realize I had that assumption until it was proven the other way around and I was legitimately surprised.

item.title: No Good Deed:
item.content:encoded: This and All Hallows' are the best things you've written that I have read thus far. I already felt like Anderson wasn't fully a villain. Now you've explored that aspect of him. (Not that he's a good guy, just that you are successful in portraying him as a multi-faceted person enough that I picked up on it before this tale.) You've hit a certain bar that assures that I have warmed up to a character forever; whenever a scene cuts off, I instinctively stop reading and imagine the continuation, or implications as they sprawl. In this case, I had a lot of faux-conversations between Anderson and others, like when he enters Merlo's house, when he says he'll "mull things over" to Shaw, or when he asks again where his brother would like to go. Good, good stuff. Really loving this character.

item.title: Bal-chatri:
item.content:encoded:
Navarro mumbled, violently shaking as he was helped to his feet a wink, the two agents watching as the worn down husk that was Vincent Anderson stumbled onto the stage.

I can not for the life of me figure out what "a wink" is doing in this sentence.

“But the company still exists. Phineas has probably taken over by now. Lop off one head and have another two grow back in its place.”

Oh god I am a sucker for thematic call-backs, and this is especially potent given that Phineas was the one who said that line. Absolutely perfect.

And oh-ho-ho damn, this was a banger of a series ender. Anderson may have "escaped" (not really), but the dynamic is quite different now, isn't it? I wonder how long he can keep control of the company before the rest of everyone decides its time he be overthrown. I mean, he can't just stay top-dog while at all times being at risk of dying or otherwise losing connection to his Saker… right? Intriguing as hell.

item.title: Realignment:
item.content:encoded: Hot damn, this was fantastic. I'm less of an action-man myself, so having a tale that was slower and more personal was exactly my speed. Great interplay between the characters, wonderful storytelling, I really like Phineas, Merlo, and am continuing to grow fond of Anderson Robotics which I had no strong feelings for before… glad to have had a Kalinin guest tale. This is great.
